It becomes doable only if an Intel .dmg is ever produced, which needs a second CI job on a billed Intel runner (see the packaging README). title: Does the macOS app launch at all? Apple silicon, 20 minutes, either answer is useful
value: This is the single most valuable unknown in the project. NOBODY HAS EVER RUN YazSes ON A MAC — not the maintainer, who develops on Linux, not a contributor, not CI. macOS CI is green, but it only proves the code imports and the dependencies resolve: the hotkey capture, the Accessibility permission and the text injector have no automated coverage, because none of them can be tested without hardware. The same repository already shipped a Windows .exe across several releases that never started its daemon, and CI proved it 'built' the whole time. Twenty minutes on any Apple silicon Mac closes that gap for macOS. A broken result is worth exactly as much as a working one.
evidence: the exact install command and the version it produced
whether the app launched at all, and what Gatekeeper said on first open (it is unsigned, so expect a warning and a right-click -> Open)
whether the Accessibility and Microphone prompts appeared, and whether you could find the settings pane
whether holding Right Option and speaking actually typed text into a window, and which app you tried it in
`yazses doctor` output with your username, hostname and home path removed
